record.paper_title: Mathematical open problems in Projected Entangled Pair States
record.original_question: For the two-dimensional global PEPS approximation problem, can the bond-dimension bound f(L) required to approximate an L by L system be chosen to grow polynomially in the linear system size L?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a two-dimensional quantum spin system on an $L \times L$ square lattice, where each site carries a finite-dimensional Hilbert space $\mathbb{C}^d$. A Projected Entangled Pair State (PEPS) on this lattice with bond dimension $D$ is a state of the form
$$|\Psi\rangle = \sum_{i_1,\dots,i_{L^2}} \mathcal{C}\bigl(A^{[1]}_{i_1}, \dots, A^{[L^2]}_{i_{L^2}}\bigr)\, |i_1 \cdots i_{L^2}\rangle,$$
where each $A^{[v]}_{i_v}$ is a tensor with one physical index $i_v \in \{1,\dots,d\}$ and four virtual indices of dimension $D$ (one per nearest-neighbor edge), and $\mathcal{C}$ denotes the contraction of all virtual indices along the edges of the lattice.

Suppose $H_L$ is a local, translationally invariant, gapped Hamiltonian on the $L\times L$ lattice with unique ground state $|\Omega_L\rangle$. Define $f(L)$ to be the smallest bond dimension such that there exists a PEPS $|\Psi_L\rangle$ with bond dimension at most $f(L)$ satisfying
$$\bigl\| |\Omega_L\rangle - |\Psi_L\rangle \bigr\| \le \varepsilon,$$
for a fixed approximation error $\varepsilon > 0$ (globally, in the full $L^2$-site Hilbert space norm).

Question: Can $f(L)$ always be chosen to grow at most polynomially in $L$? Equivalently, does every gapped local 2D Hamiltonian admit a PEPS approximation of its ground state with bond dimension polynomial in the linear system size?
artifact.status_search_result: The question of whether ground states of 2D gapped local Hamiltonians can be globally approximated by PEPS with bond dimension polynomial in the linear size remains an active open problem. The 1D analogue (MPS approximation for gapped 1D systems) is established, but its 2D PEPS extension is unresolved; a 2D area law alone is not known to imply polynomial-bond-dimension PEPS approximation, and recent work (e.g., on 2D area laws for frustration-free systems, ~2023–2024) frames it as still open.

status_evidence.title: An Area Law for 2D Frustration-Free Spin Systems
status_evidence.snippet: Whether ground states of locally gapped frustration-free systems admit efficient tensor-network (PEPS) approximations is highlighted as open.
status_evidence.claim: Polynomial-bond-dimension PEPS approximation in 2D is still an open question.

status_evidence.title: Computational complexity of injective projected entangled pair states
status_evidence.snippet: Studies of PEPS complexity continue, with global approximation properties not fully resolved.
status_evidence.claim: Foundational approximation properties of PEPS in 2D remain under investigation.
